$comment: GENERATED FILE — DO NOT EDIT. Produced by scripts/buildCliHelp.ts from the JSDoc above each route() in src/cli/engine/routes. Edit the comment on the route, then run `npm run prepare` (or `npm run docs:api`).

accelerate.description: Replace-by-fee, where the plugin supports it. Returns a new unsigned transaction to sign and broadcast.

params.objectId: Handle of the transaction to bump.

accelerate.returnsDoc: Given objectId the same handle is updated; given a transaction a new one is created.
notes: A plugin that cannot accelerate returns 400 rather than a null transaction.

account-info.description: Session fields are spread at the top level alongside the account's own properties — there is no nested `session` object.

returns.recoveryKey: string | null — Present only while recovery is configured.
returns.otpResetPending: boolean — True while somebody has a reset pending against this account.
returns.edgeLogin: boolean — This account was reached by QR login.

notes: The `otpEnabled` and `otpResetPending` flags here are derived. For the secret itself use `otp-key`.

admin-auth-request.description: Sends an arbitrary request with the context's credentials attached. Debugging only — this is core's private surface.

params.path: Login-server path, not an engine path.
params.body: Request body, when the method takes one.

admin-hash-username.description: Reproduces the login server's hashing, to derive a login id offline.

returns.ok: boolean — Always true; a failure arrives as an error envelope.

notes: Not under `/account/{sessionId}/objects/`, because admin lobbies belong to no session.

admin-make-lobby.description: A lobby polls the login server until closed, so the engine parks it under a `lobby_` handle and closes it on expiry rather than leaking the poll.

returns.replies: unknown[] — Empty at creation; re-read to see replies.

notes: Release it with `admin-lobby-handle-delete`, or the poll runs for the full five minutes.

admin-repo-delete.description: Destructive, and not undoable from this API.

params.path: Subdirectory. Defaults to the repo root.

returns.listing: unknown — Path to entry type: `file` or `folder`.

admin-repo-set.description: Writes directly into a synced repo, bypassing every core-level invariant. A malformed write can break the account for real clients.

all-keys.summary: List every key in the account.
all-keys.description: Includes archived and deleted keys, unlike `currency-wallets`.

returns.allKeys: unknown[] — `EdgeWalletInfoFull[]`: id, type, keys, archived, deleted, hidden, sortIndex.

approve-login-request.description: Grants the requesting device access to this account.

params.lobbyId: From the QR code, or an `edge://edge/<lobbyId>` link.

returns.ok: boolean — Always true; a failure arrives as an error envelope.

notes: The lobby is re-fetched on approve, so a request that expired between inspecting and approving fails with `404 NO_LOGIN_REQUEST`.

approve-swap-quote.description: Moves funds. The handle is released afterwards whether or not the response is read, so record `orderId` from it.

returns.objectId: string — The handle that was consumed.
returns.orderId: unknown — The exchange's order reference, when it gives one.
returns.transaction: unknown — The on-chain send to the exchange.

notes: The plugin attaches its own savedAction and assetAction metadata; the engine adds none.

approve-voucher.description: Lets the waiting device finish logging in.

balance-map.summary: Balances for every asset in the wallet.
balance-map.description: The native currency plus every enabled token.

returns.balances: { tokenId: string | null; currencyCode: string; nativeAmount: string; displayAmount: string; }[]

notes: On the CLI, omit `--token-id` for the native asset rather than passing the literal `null`.

broadcast-tx.description: The irreversible step: once this returns, the funds have left the wallet.
broadcast-tx.returnsDoc: The handle survives, so `save-tx` can still run.
notes: Broadcasting does not record the transaction locally. Follow with `save-tx`, or it stays missing from history until a sync finds it.

cancel-otp-reset.description: The defence against somebody else requesting a reset on your account: as long as you cancel before the timer runs out, their reset never lands.

notes: If the login already completed and a session exists, that session is force-logged-out too, so cancelling cannot leave an orphan visible in `engine-sessions`.

change-enabled-token-ids.description: Absolute: anything missing from `tokenIds` is disabled. Core has only this setter, so there is no add or remove call.
notes: The command's `--add` and `--remove` are client-side sugar over this one route, and cost an extra read first.

change-password.description: The login server enforces its own rules; `check-password-rules` scores a candidate first.

change-paused.summary: Pause or resume a wallet engine.
change-paused.description: A paused wallet stops syncing, which is how a caller quiets a chain it does not currently care about.

params.enableLogin: Allow logging in with this PIN on this device.
params.forDuressAccount: Act on the duress account rather than the real one.

returns.pin2Key: string — The new PIN login key core returns.

change-recovery.description: The returned key is half of the credential: without it the answers alone cannot recover the account, so it has to be stored somewhere else.

returns.recoveryKey: string — Store this out of band. `login-with-recovery` needs it alongside the answers.

change-username.description: The old name is released, so it becomes available to anyone else.

params.password: Required by core when the account has a password.

change-wallet-states.summary: Archive, delete, hide, or reorder wallets.
change-wallet-states.description: The canonical backend for every wallet flag; there are no separate archive, unarchive or undelete verbs.

params.walletStates: `EdgeWalletStates`: wallet ids to the flags being changed.

check-password.description: Checks without changing anything, which is how a caller gates a destructive action behind a re-entry prompt.

returns.ok: boolean — False for a wrong password — not an error response.

check-password-rules.returnsDoc: `EdgePasswordRules` from core: passed, tooShort, noNumber, noLowerCase, noUpperCase, secondsToCrack.
notes: Send it with `curl --get --data-urlencode` rather than putting it in a shell-visible URL.

params.pin: The device PIN, usually four digits.
params.forDuressAccount: Act on the duress account rather than the real one.

returns.ok: boolean — False for a wrong PIN — not an error response.

close-swap-quote.description: Closes the plugin object without executing, freeing whatever the exchange was holding.

create-account.description: Every credential is optional over REST: omitting all three creates a light account with no username.

params.otpKey: The 2FA secret itself, instead of a code.
params.challengeId: Supply after solving a CAPTCHA to retry the same request.

notes: The command requires a username, password and PIN. Creating a light account is REST-only.

params.name: Display name.
params.importText: Seed or key text to import instead of generating.

notes: `fiatCurrencyCode` and `importText` are REST-only; the command has no flags for them.

create-currency-wallets.description: Partial success is normal: each entry reports its own outcome, and one failure does not roll back the others.

returns.results: unknown[] — Mirrors core's EdgeResult[]: `{ ok, wallet }` or `{ ok: false, error }`.

create-wallet.summary: Create a wallet from raw key JSON.
create-wallet.description: The import path. Use `create-currency-wallet` to make a fresh wallet with generated keys.

params.keys: Plugin key material. Omit to let core generate it.

currency-configs.summary: List plugin ids usable for wallet creation.
currency-configs.description: Currency and accountbased plugins only — swap plugins are excluded.

params.waitForAll: Await every wallet to load first. Without it a freshly logged-in account may report fewer wallets than it has.

returns.currencyWallets: { walletId: string; id: string; type: string; name: string | null; pluginId: string; currencyCode: string; fiatCurrencyCode: string; blockHeight: number; syncStatus: unknown; syncRatio: string | undefined; paused: boolean; imported: boolean | undefined; created: string | null; enabledTokenIds: string[]; detectedTokenIds: string[]; unactivatedTokenIds: string[]; }[]

notes: The REST default for `waitForAll` is false; the command defaults it to true. A raw HTTP caller that skips it can see an incomplete list.

params.storeId: Plugin or app namespace within the account data store.

delete-password.description: The account keeps its other login methods; only the password stops working.

delete-pin.description: PIN login stops working on this device; other methods are untouched.

delete-recovery.description: The existing recovery key stops working.

delete-remote-account.description: Irreversible. The account is removed from the login server, and funds in its wallets are unrecoverable without the keys. The session is logged out afterwards.
notes: The engine performs no confirmation check — the call runs as soon as it arrives, so any guard has to live in the caller. The command requires `--yes` for exactly this reason.

delete-store.description: Removes every item in it, which cannot be undone from this API.

params.storeId: Plugin or app namespace within the account data store.

disable-otp.description: Logins stop requiring a code immediately.

dump-data.description: Plugin-defined debug output. Shape varies by plugin and can be very large.

enable-otp.description: Record the returned key before leaving the terminal: it is the only copy.

params.timeout: How long a reset request must wait before it completes. Core supplies the default when omitted.

returns.otpKey: string | null — The new secret. The 2FA secret itself. Secret material — record it safely.

encode-uri.description: For a receive screen or a QR code.

params.label: BIP21 `label`; becomes `metadata.name` when parsed back.
params.currencyCode: Disambiguates on chains that carry several assets.

returns.uri: string — The encoded URI, ready for a QR code.

notes: Only these five fields are read; a fuller `EdgeEncodeUri` has its extras ignored.

engine-config.description: What the engine passed to `makeEdgeContext`. Contains no secrets. Use it to assert tester hosts before a test run.
notes: Outside `-t` / `--test`, `servers` is an empty object — core is using its built-in production defaults, so there is nothing to echo back.

engine-sessions.returnsDoc: A bare array, not wrapped in a key.

engine-status.description: The readiness probe the client polls after auto-spawning the engine.
engine-status.returnsDoc: `idleShutdownAt` is null while a session or a subscription holds the engine open, and `tcpPort` is null unless started with `--tcp`.

engine-stop.description: Logs out every session, closes the context, unlinks the socket and run-file, then exits. The engine answers before it starts tearing down, so a response is not proof the process is gone.

returns.ok: boolean — Always true; a failure arrives as an error envelope.

notes: In-flight callers may see `503 ENGINE_SHUTTING_DOWN` once teardown starts.

fetch-challenge.description: Lets a client solve a challenge before it hits `403 CHALLENGE_REQUIRED` mid-flow.
fetch-challenge.returnsDoc: `challengeUri` is absent when the server considers the challenge already satisfied.

fetch-lobby.description: The other side of `request-edge-login`: shows who is asking, so a human can decide before approving.

params.lobbyId: From the QR code, or an `edge://edge/<lobbyId>` link.

returns.loginRequest: { appId: string; displayName: string; displayImageDarkUrl: string | null; displayImageLightUrl: string | null; } | null — Null when the lobby carries no pending login request.

fetch-login-messages.summary: Fetch login-server messages for every local user.
fetch-login-messages.returnsDoc: `EdgeLoginMessages` from core, keyed by loginId; each value carries otpResetPending and pendingVouchers.

params.recoveryKey: From `change-recovery`, stored by the user out of band.

fetch-swap-quotes.description: Polls every enabled swap plugin and parks each result under its own `swap_` handle with a 5 minute TTL.

params.fromWalletId: Source wallet. Accepts a unique prefix.
params.quoteFor: `from` spends this much of the source, `to` receives this much at the destination, `max` sends everything. Defaults to `from`.

returns.quotes: { objectId: string; kind: string; expiresAt: string; pluginId: string; isEstimate: boolean; canBePartial: boolean | null; maxFulfillmentSeconds: number | null; minReceiveAmount: string | null; fromNativeAmount: string; toNativeAmount: string; networkFee: { nativeAmount: any; tokenId: any; }; quoteExpirationDate: string | null; swapInfo: { pluginId: any; displayName: any; supportEmail: any; isDex: any; }; request: { fromTokenId: any; toTokenId: any; nativeAmount: any; quoteFor: any; fromWalletId: any; toWalletId: any; }; }[]

notes: Every returned quote holds an open plugin object. Approving one releases only that handle; close the rest, or let them expire.
An empty `quotes` array with `quoteCount: 0` is a success, not an error — no plugin could serve the pair.

fix-username.description: Applies the same rules the login server does, so a caller can show the user what their name will actually be before creating an account.

returns.username: string — The normalized value. The input is not echoed.

forget-account.summary: Forget an account on this device.
forget-account.description: Removes locally cached credentials. The remote account is untouched.

params.rootLoginId: Core takes a `rootLoginId`. A username is also accepted and resolved against `localUsers` first, so callers need not hash it.

get-display-private-key.summary: Export the private key for display.
get-display-private-key.description: Secret. The human-facing form — WIF, seed phrase, whatever the plugin shows on its export screen.

get-display-public-key.summary: Export the public key for display.
get-display-public-key.description: The xpub or equivalent — safe to share for watch-only use.

get-item.description: Values are opaque strings; encoding is the caller's business.

params.storeId: Plugin or app namespace within the account data store.

get-login-key.description: The key `login-with-key` takes. It grants full account access, so treat the output as secret.

returns.loginKey: string — base58. Full account access — keep it safe.

get-max-spendable.description: What empties the wallet after fees. A destination is still required, since fees depend on it.

params.spendInfo: A full `EdgeSpendInfo`, used as-is when present.
params.to: Address or BIP21 URI, run through `wallet.parseUri`.
params.metadata: Wins over anything parsed out of the URI.

returns.nativeAmount: string — The most this wallet can send.

get-num-transactions.description: Cheaper than listing when only the total matters.

returns.numTransactions: number — Every transaction the wallet knows of.

notes: Unfiltered: `spamThreshold`, dates and `searchString` do not apply, so this can exceed `total` from `get-transactions`.

get-payment-protocol-info.description: Feed `spendTargets` from the result into `make-spend` to pay it.

get-pin.description: Returns the PIN itself, not a status flag, so treat the output as secret.

returns.pin: string | null — Null when no PIN is set.

get-raw-private-key.description: Secret. Whatever the plugin stores — seed, mnemonic, xpriv.
get-raw-private-key.returnsDoc: The plugin's key object, at the top level.

get-transactions.summary: List or export a wallet's transactions.
get-transactions.description: Reads history, overlays the display metadata the GUI shows, fills historical fiat, and optionally formats the result — all on this one call.

params.limit: Omitting it returns every transaction from `offset` on.
params.searchString: Matches payee, category, notes and txid.
params.spamThreshold: Native-amount floor. Omitted, the account spam-filter setting applies; passing it always overrides.
params.fiat: Three-letter ISO 4217 code. Defaults to the account defaultIsoFiat.

get-transactions.returnsDoc: `{ transactions, total, isoFiat }`, or `{ ok, isoFiat, total, files }` when exportFormat is set.
notes: The metadata overlay and the fiat fill are response-only. Neither writes to disk.
`limit` and `offset` apply before the fiat fill, so a large page costs proportionally more rates-server work.
This is the one GET that can write: passing `bitwaveAccountId` persists it to `exportTxInfo.json` on the wallet disklet.

get-wallet-info.returnsDoc: `EdgeWalletInfoFull`, verbatim from core — including the `keys` object.
notes: An exact lookup: unlike the wallet-scoped routes this does not accept an id prefix.

list-item-ids.summary: List item ids in a store.

params.storeId: Plugin or app namespace within the account data store.

list-splittable-wallet-types.summary: List chains a wallet can split into.
list-splittable-wallet-types.description: Forked-chain support: which wallet types can be derived from these keys.

list-store-ids.description: The account's synced key-value store, where plugins keep their own state.

local-settings.description: Writes device-local account settings. Every option is a field on the body; `spamFilterOn` is the only one today, and new options are added alongside it.

params.spamFilterOn: Hide spam transactions in `get-transactions` results. Defaults to `true`, matching the GUI. The filter hides rows; it never changes stored metadata.

returns.spamFilterOn: boolean — Hide spam transactions in `get-transactions` results. Defaults to `true`, matching the GUI. The filter hides rows; it never changes stored metadata.

notes: Omitting a field is a `400`, not a no-op, so a caller cannot clear a setting by accident.

local-users.summary: List local users on this device.
local-users.returnsDoc: Everything `context.localUsers` reports, including which login methods each user has enabled on this device.

login-with-key.summary: Log in with an account login key.
login-with-key.description: The key comes from `get-login-key` on an already-authenticated session.

params.otpKey: The 2FA secret itself, instead of a code.
params.challengeId: Supply after solving a CAPTCHA to retry the same request.
params.usernameOrLoginId: A username, or a login id.
params.useLoginId: Treat the value as a login id.

params.otpKey: The 2FA secret itself, instead of a code.
params.challengeId: Supply after solving a CAPTCHA to retry the same request.

notes: With `--solve-captcha` the client solves a `CHALLENGE_REQUIRED` response headlessly (ALTCHA proof-of-work) and retries once.

login-with-pin.summary: Log in with a device PIN.
login-with-pin.description: Only works on a device that has already saved a PIN for the account.

params.otpKey: The 2FA secret itself, instead of a code.
params.challengeId: Supply after solving a CAPTCHA to retry the same request.
params.usernameOrLoginId: A username, or a login id.
params.useLoginId: Treat the value as a login id.

login-with-recovery.description: Needs both the recovery key and the answers; neither works alone.

params.otpKey: The 2FA secret itself, instead of a code.
params.challengeId: Supply after solving a CAPTCHA to retry the same request.
params.answers: In the same order as the questions.

logout.description: Ends the session and drops it from the engine. Any subscription scoped to this account or its wallets is closed with it.

make-spend.description: First step of the staged workflow: nothing is signed and no funds move. Inspect `transaction.networkFee` on the result before signing.

params.spendInfo: A full `EdgeSpendInfo`, used as-is when present.
params.to: Address or BIP21 URI, run through `wallet.parseUri`.
params.metadata: Wins over anything parsed out of the URI.

object-delete.description: Runs the handle's cleanup — closing a swap quote, cancelling a pending login — instead of waiting out the TTL.

object-get.description: Works for every kind: transactions, pending logins, swap quotes.
object-get.returnsDoc: The handle fields, plus a `value` holding the live core object.
notes: Reading does not extend the TTL. Only a step that updates the value does.

otp-key.summary: Read the 2FA secret and reset state.

returns.otpKey: string | null — Null when 2FA is off. The 2FA secret itself. Secret material — record it safely.
returns.otpResetDate: string | null — Set once somebody has requested a reset; cancel it with `cancel-otp-reset`.

parse-uri.summary: Parse a payment URI or address.
parse-uri.description: What the GUI address tile does when you paste or scan something.

params.uri: A payment URI or a bare address.
params.currencyCode: Disambiguates on chains that carry several assets.

notes: `spend` and `make-spend` run their `to` field through this same call, so parsing separately is only needed to inspect or confirm first.

pending-vouchers.description: When 2FA blocks a login, the login server issues a voucher that an already-trusted device can approve or reject.

returns.pendingVouchers: unknown[] — `EdgePendingVoucher[]`: voucherId, activates, created, deviceDescription, ipDescription.

rates-query.summary: Batch crypto and fiat rate lookups.
rates-query.description: Concurrent lookups share one rates-server queue, so asking for many rates at once costs a single upstream request.

returns.crypto: { pluginId: string; tokenId: string | null; targetFiat: string; date: string; rate: number; }[] — Always present; empty when no crypto rates were requested.
returns.fiat: { fiatCode: string; targetFiat: string; date: string; rate: number; }[]

notes: A rate the server cannot supply comes back as `0` rather than an error, so check for zero before dividing.

rates-usd-to-native.summary: Convert a USD amount into native units.
rates-usd-to-native.description: Turns a fiat notional into the native amount a spend needs.

params.usdAmount: A string, which must parse to a positive finite number.
params.multiplier: Native units per whole coin. Defaults per plugin.
params.date: ISO-8601. Omitted, the current time is sent to the rates server.

returns.usdAmount: number — Echoed as a number, though it is sent as a string.
returns.rate: number — USD per whole coin at that date.
returns.displayAmount: string — Whole coins, to 8 decimal places.
returns.nativeAmount: string — What a spend actually takes.

notes: `displayAmount` is rounded to 8 decimals before conversion, so assets with finer precision lose the tail. For an exact figure use `rates-query` and do the arithmetic yourself.
Default multipliers cover bitcoin, ethereum, bitcoincash, litecoin and dogecoin; pass `multiplier` explicitly for anything else.

reject-voucher.description: Denies the waiting device. The login it was issued for cannot complete.

repair-otp.summary: Re-point the account at a known 2FA secret.
repair-otp.description: For a device whose stored secret has drifted from the server's.

params.otpKey: The secret the account should use.

request-edge-login.description: Asks the login server for a lobby another logged-in Edge device can approve. The returned `lobbyId` is what goes in the QR code.

returns.session: { sessionId: string; username: string | undefined; rootLoginId: string; loginMethod: "password" | "pin" | "key" | "recovery" | "edge" | "create"; autoLogoutSeconds: number; expiresAt: string | null; lastActivityAt: string; createdAt: string; } | null

notes: The pending login is an object handle with a 5 minute TTL. On expiry the engine cancels the request on the login server for you.

request-otp-reset.description: Starts the timed reset a user falls back on after losing their authenticator.
request-otp-reset.returnsDoc: When the reset completes if nobody cancels it.

resync-blockchain.description: Drops cached chain state and re-scans. Expensive, and the wallet reports an incomplete balance until it finishes.
notes: Returns when the resync is requested, not when it completes. Watch `syncRatio` for progress.

save-tx.summary: Record a transaction and release its handle.
save-tx.description: Final step. The handle is gone afterwards, so a second call is a 404.

params.objectId: The handle to persist and release.

save-tx-action.description: Records what a transaction *was* — a swap, a stake — beyond its metadata.
notes: When `assetAction` is omitted it defaults to `{ assetActionType: 'transfer' }`.

save-tx-metadata.description: One of only two routes that write transaction metadata to disk.
notes: `metadata` is an `EdgeMetadataChange`, so an explicit null clears a field while an omitted one is left alone.

set-fiat-currency-code.description: Affects how balances and history are priced, not the asset itself.

set-item.description: Creates the store if it does not exist.

params.storeId: Plugin or app namespace within the account data store.

sign-bytes.description: Message signing and proof-of-ownership, for plugins that support it.

params.bytes: Base64. Defaults to empty when absent.

notes: Invalid base64 decodes to empty rather than erroring, so validate before sending.

sign-tx.description: Keeps the same handle and pushes its expiry out another five minutes.

spend.description: `makeSpend`, then `signTx`, then optionally `broadcastTx` and `saveTx`, in one request. `broadcast` and `save` both default to true, so a bare body with a destination and an amount moves real money. A completed spend leaves no handle behind.

params.spendInfo: A full `EdgeSpendInfo`, used as-is when present.
params.to: Address or BIP21 URI, run through `wallet.parseUri`.
params.metadata: Wins over anything parsed out of the URI.
params.useMax: Replace the first target's amount with the maximum.
params.dryRun: Build only. Never signs or broadcasts.

spend.returnsDoc: `{ transaction }`, plus `saveError` when the broadcast succeeded but saving failed. With dryRun, a TransactionHandle instead.
notes: BIP21 `label` and `message` from `to` become metadata name and notes. An explicit `metadata` object wins.

`saveError` is the case to handle. Once broadcast, the money is gone, so a failure inside saveTx cannot throw — it would hide the txid of a real payment. The response is 200 with the transaction plus `saveError`.
With `dryRun`, only makeSpend runs and the response is a transaction handle that expires in 5 minutes.

split.summary: Split a wallet into another chain.
split.description: Forked-chain support: derive a wallet of a different type from the same keys. `list-splittable-wallet-types` says which are valid.

returns.results: unknown[] — Per-entry outcomes, like batch create.

subscribe.description:
Holds a Server-Sent Events stream open until the caller disconnects or the engine closes it. Runs concurrently with one-shot calls, so a subscriber in one terminal watches what another terminal does.

A live subscription holds the engine open past its idle timeout. It does not hold an account logged in: the auto-logout timer still fires, and closes any subscription scoped to that account or one of its wallets. Context-scoped subscriptions survive, because the context outlives every account.

returns.data: unknown — Payload, shaped by the event type.

subscribe.returnsDoc: One frame per event, as `event:` then `data:` lines.
notes: Frame types: `core.log`, `session.created`, `session.expired`, `engine.shutdown`, and `subscription.closed` when the engine ends it.
`sessionId` in event payloads is truncated to its first 10 characters.
A client more than 1 MiB behind is disconnected rather than buffered.
Served directly by the HTTP handler rather than through the router, because the response never ends.

returns.swapInfo: { pluginId: string; displayName: string; supportEmail: string; isDex: boolean | null; }
returns.request: { fromTokenId: string | null; toTokenId: string | null; nativeAmount: string; quoteFor: "to" | "from" | "max"; fromWalletId: string; toWalletId: string; }

notes: Check `quoteExpirationDate` as well as `expiresAt`: the plugin's price can go stale before the handle does.

sweep-private-keys.summary: Sweep private keys into this wallet.
sweep-private-keys.description: Builds a transaction moving everything from an external key. Returns an unsigned handle: sign, broadcast and save it like any staged spend.

params.spendInfo: A full `EdgeSpendInfo`, with the keys to sweep in `privateKeys`.

sync.description: Pushes and pulls the account repos immediately rather than waiting for the next scheduled sync.

touch.description: Resets the idle auto-logout timer without doing any other work.

username-available.summary: Check whether a username is free.

params.challengeId: Supply after solving a CAPTCHA to retry the same check.

wallet-info.returnsDoc: Every WalletSummary field, plus denominations, walletSettings and allTokens.

notes: Named `wallet-sync` on the CLI because `sync` is `account.sync`.

wallet-tokens.description: "Enabled" tokens are the ones the wallet syncs balances for; "detected" ones were seen on-chain but are not yet enabled.

returns.allTokens: { [keys: string]: unknown; } — Built-in and custom together, keyed by tokenId. Large on EVM chains.
returns.detectedTokenIds: string[] — Seen on-chain but not enabled, so their balances are not synced.
